interpretation.requestedResult: Find both the glass refractive index and small prism apex angle using a transmitted-beam 1° deviation and a two-reflection/return beam 4° deviation from the reversed incidence.
stated: Parallel incident beam is normal to the first face of a prism of small refracting angle.
At the second face the beam is partly transmitted and partly reflected; reflected beam returns to first face and emerges.
Returning emerging ray is at 4° to the reversed incident direction.
Transmitted beam deviates by 1° from original incident direction.
unknowns: Current native planar interfaces are parallel; a nonparallel two-face prism with internal reflection/transmission, inverse glass index and apex angle is not an available deterministic requested operation.
No finite prism shape, source brightness or signed branch is supplied; do not invent one to create a misleading simulation.

interpretation.requestedResult: Find apparent depth below the glass sphere surface of a small air bubble viewed radially from outside.
stated: Glass sphere refractive index 1.5 and radius 15.0 cm.
Tiny air bubble lies 5 cm above the sphere center.
Viewing direction is downward along the extended radius containing the bubble.
derived: Along the stated radial axis the true distance from the nearest surface to the bubble is 15−5=10 cm.
unknowns: The imaging boundary is curved glass/air and requires spherical refraction; existing planar media and ideal thin-lens/reflective elements cannot faithfully provide the apparent-depth operation.
Do not substitute a plane interface or a mirror merely to return an easy numerical result.

cases.firstScopeAssessment: Curved dielectric refraction and apparent-depth image location are not implemented. Stated true geometric depth is not the apparent-depth answer; no native scene proposed.
